title: Nine Inches of Cloth
subtitle: 帽子与瓶盖 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 帽子与瓶盖（生活与学习·服饰与器物）
meta: 主题语境：帽子与瓶盖（生活与学习·服饰与器物）　|　核心词汇：cap　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cap 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my mother was sent to fit ① a cap she could not wear, and she said the wearing was the whole of the lesson. The ② cap, meaning the cloth and not the badge, was nine inches wide and was worn by whoever came last; a cap, she said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ cap in that cupboard had the same peak, and the ④ cap at the front, meaning the one the porter wore and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever fitted properly. A cap, my grandmother said, is nine parts cloth and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the cloth is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cap was the whole of the rank, meaning the rank it showed and not the cloth. The ⑥ cap, meaning the rank and not any of that, is the only thing in a regiment that everybody salutes and nobody questions; a cap, he said, is either something you fit or the only word that means both a cloth and a rank. She said the rank is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ cap had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the peak. The ⑧ cap of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine inches and eleven years of fitting; a cap, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cap I remember is the one at the front, which was worn out in 1970 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ cap, my grandmother said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being worn; every cap, she said, is a rank that has agreed to look like a cloth. She said the rank was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 帽子（指那块布本身，与徽章相对）
C. 固定搭配：fit a cap 给（某人）试戴帽子／配帽
D. n. 帽子（指柜子里每一顶）
E. n. 帽子（指前面那一顶）
F. n. 帽子（抽象：它表示的那个级别）
G. n. 那个级别（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a cap she could not wear
The cap, meaning the cloth and not the badge
cap was the whole of the rank
the cap had become a photograph in a report
The cap of the whole thing
A cap, my grandmother said in 1974

answers.why: fit a cap 意为“给（某人）试戴帽子／配帽”，1948 年母亲被派去配一顶她戴不上的帽子。
cap 意为“帽子”，指那块布本身而不是徽章，宽九英寸，由最后走的人戴着。
cap 指柜子里每一顶帽子，每一顶都是同样的帽檐。
cap 指前面那一顶（门房戴的那一顶），是唯一有人认真配过的。
cap 意为“帽子”，抽象指它表示的那个级别，父亲说 cap 就是那个级别的全部。
cap 为抽象用法，指那个级别本身，是团里人人都敬礼、却没人质疑的东西。
cap 意为“帽子、盖”，到 1965 年这顶 cap 成了报告里的一张照片。
cap 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英寸和十一年的配帽。
cap 意为“帽子”，我记得的是前面那一顶，1970 年戴坏，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
cap 为抽象总称，祖母说帽子是唯一会因为被戴旧而变好的东西。
